title: Canonical closed mate and braiding of condensed derived restriction
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f:Y\to X$ a weakly étale morphism of schemes. Assume the canonical coefficient pullback map is invertible [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Equip the actual left-derived internal-module pullback $F=\mathbf Lf^*$ with its existing canonical monoidal structure [lem-sfb-derived-pullback-strong-monoidal]. For arbitrary unbounded derived modules $K,N$, the canonical internal-Hom comparison $F(R\mathcal Hom(K,N))\to R\mathcal Hom(FK,FN)$, namely ihomComparison, is invertible. Its actual tensorator satisfies $\mu_{K,N}; F(\beta_{K,N})=\beta_{FK,FN};\mu_{N,K}$, where composition is read in diagrammatic order and $\beta$ denotes the native derived Koszul braiding.

proof.text: On the slice, exact restriction preserves K-injective representatives and the internal Hom complex. Its tensor and Hom comparisons preserve the actual counit for arbitrary unbounded inputs. Transport these comparisons through the normalized section equivalence.

The derived-counit characterization identifies the transported tensor comparison with the existing K-flat pullback tensorator. Koszul interchange commutes with termwise restriction and descends to the stated braiding equation. The counit identity says that the transported Hom isomorphism is the canonical mate ihomComparison, proving its invertibility.

lean.statement:
theorem proetale_derived_restriction_closed
    (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u}) [IsCommMonObj Λ.X]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [WeaklyEtale f]
    [IsIso (condensedPullbackHom Λ.X f)] :
    let d := nativeDerivedRestrictionData Λ f
    let F := d.functor
    letI := d.monoidal
    (∀ K N : DerivedCategory (Internal Λ.X X),
      IsIso ((Functor.LaxMonoidal.ihomComparison F K).natTrans.app N)) ∧
    (∀ K N : DerivedCategory (Internal Λ.X X),
      Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ F K N ≫ F.map (β_ K N).hom =
        (β_ (F.obj K) (F.obj N)).hom ≫ Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ F N K)
